purpose: Which flow reads and writes which portal list, what crosses into the internal estate and where, and what is not yet wired. Derived from the 01-09 design as the SPOT workbook reads it out of those definitions, expressed against live list GUIDs, and checked against the flows actually deployed.
principle: The portal estate is a trust boundary. Its flows are invoked by anonymous strangers with no session, so they may touch the twelve portal lists and nothing else. Exactly one crossing exists - ECM_DOCS_INTAKE - and the property that protects it is that it is TENANT-AUTHENTICATED, not that it is read-only: it reads the portal registry outward for the internal platform and, under D1, writes portal status back. It touches no internal list in either direction, and no anonymous caller can invoke it at all. No portal flow may read or write the internal operations estate or any DGO_* governance list.

endpoints.purpose: Register a submission, mint its reference, and issue one upload ticket per declared attachment.

referenceMinting.mustNotUse: concat('NITDA-', yyyy, '-', last 3 digits of ticks(utcNow())) - the deployed expression. A thousand values per year drawn at random; a collision is more likely than not after about thirty-seven submissions.
referenceMinting.why: The legacy references are never persisted and no flow looks them up, so nothing depends on the old format. Minting sequentially from the counter, at a width the legacy form never used, keeps the two generations distinguishable to a person while both are in circulation during the deferred migration.

telemetry.why: The house standard already composes the record in 23 flows and ships it by email. This gives it a queryable home. One create per run, in the capture scope, not on the request path.

endpoints.requiredOperationsCorrection: A Portal Registry `update` was required here and is removed 2026-09-03. Nothing performs it and nothing needs to: Create_Submission_Record writes the COMPLETE row in one call — Title, ReferenceId, Subject, Category, CorrespondenceType, Channel, the five sender fields, EventDate, Description, AttachmentCount, SubmittedAtUtc, UpdatedAtUtc, Status, StatusLabel, ActionRequired, VerifiedSubmission, SourceIp and LocalId. The reference is minted BEFORE the create, so there is no second pass to write it back. Checked in all three places a create-then-update would have to appear: the deployed definition exported 2026-09-03, the Portal_SUBMISSION_ECM_DOCS paste package, and the 01-portal-submission design. None has one. Adding a no-op PatchItem to a live flow to satisfy a checklist would be worse than the gap it closed.

bridge.why: The single crossing between the public estate and the internal platform, and the only one. It is tenant-authenticated, read-only, and projects a fixed column set - so the portal estate can be written by anonymous callers without any of it becoming reachable from, or reaching into, the internal operations or governance estates.

writesBack.why: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE is a live read feed, not a copy, so a portal submission has no internal row to trigger on - the four flows that create in the internal estate never read Portal Registry. A trigger-based design would need a persistence path built first. Extending the crossing costs one flow edit and one config key, and keeps the number of crossings at one.
writesBack.backwardCompatible: Callers that send no action keep today's feed behaviour.

retainedRecords.position: Remain in place. No migration, copy, rewrite or delete. Handled as a separate records-management exercise once provisioning concludes.
retainedRecords.riskAssessed: Nil for the cutover. The deployed SUBMISSION never persists the reference it mints (Update_file_properties patches id alone), and the deployed STATUS carries no $filter and never queries by reference or email - so there is no citizen-facing lookup over these records to preserve or to break.

buildStandard.position: Every action added by the remediation goes inside the standard skeleton - the work in Scope_<Purpose> under Scope_Global, the failure path in the catch scope, the answer through the standard response envelope, and the run record in Scope_Flow_Data_Capture. The portal flows adopted the response envelope and skipped the rest; 2 of 11 have Scope_Global, 1 of 11 has a catch scope, 1 of 11 redacts headers or queries.

scopeNote: WRITEBACK was added at version 1.5.0 by sponsor decision D11. Portal Audit Events, previously the one provisioned list with no reader or writer in the design, is written by it - which is why the reserved count is now zero.
unwiredListsNote: Derived by scripts/verify-portal-wiring.mjs from the endpoints' own required operations, not asserted here. It was asserted once and went stale the moment WRITEBACK began writing Portal Audit Events.

declaredCrossings.appliesToEndpointsWhy: D16 accepts this crossing for all seven portal endpoints, and the seven designer-paste packages all carry it. The prose in `decision` and `reach` said so already; this states it in a form the boundary check can read, so a crossing appearing in a package that is NOT on this list fails the gate before anyone pastes it.
declaredCrossings.measuredBy: node scripts/verify-portal-wiring.mjs, against the deployed definition exported 2026-08-31
declaredCrossings.what: The deployed CG_Writeback_Endpoint reads its allowed CORS origins from Flow Configuration, which sits on the internal operations site. WRITEBACK is invoked by anonymous callers.
declaredCrossings.contradicts: This specification's own principle, verbatim: 'No portal flow may read or write the internal operations estate or any DGO_* governance list.' The read is of the internal operations estate. The principle admits no exception for reads.
declaredCrossings.reach: All seven portal designer-paste packages read the same list for the same value, so applying them extends this from one deployed endpoint to all seven. Seven internal packages and the ECM_DOCS_INTAKE bridge also read it, but those are tenant-authenticated and already inside the internal estate, so the principle does not speak to them.
declaredCrossings.whyItIsNotNothing: The value read is public by nature — an allowed origin is a scheme and a host that every response already announces in its own header. The risk is not the value, it is the connection: the flow's SharePoint connection is authorised against the internal operations site as a whole, not against one list, so any flaw that lets a caller influence what the flow reads reaches further than this one row. That is why the principle is stated absolutely rather than per-value.
declaredCrossings.whyItIsNotUrgent: Nothing reads back to the caller. The origin is used to populate a response header, the read is chained on all statuses and fails closed, and no portal response returns list content from this read.
declaredCrossings.decision: Accepted 2026-08-31 by the agency, recorded as D16. The value is public by nature, nothing from the read reaches the caller, the read fails closed, and the deployed endpoint already does this in production — so declining would leave six endpoints on older behaviour while the seventh kept crossing. Accepted for all seven portal endpoints, since all seven packages read the same list for the same value.
declaredCrossings.boundedTo: One list, one operation, one column: Flow Configuration, read, the ALLOWED_ORIGIN_* rows. Any other list, any write, or any read whose target a caller can influence is not covered and reopens the question. No secret is ever placed in this list.
declaredCrossings.reverses: Evidence that the read target can be influenced by a caller, or a decision to scope the portal flows' SharePoint connection to the portal estate — at which point moving the origins becomes the cheaper option.

principleNote: declaredCrossings records every measured touch by a portal flow outside the twelve portal lists, whether or not it is accepted. A crossing with state UNRESOLVED is a violation of the principle above that has been seen and named, not one that has been permitted; ACCEPTED means a decision record says why, and the principle above is NOT amended — it stands as written, with each accepted crossing a named exception to it. tests/portal-wiring.test.mjs measures the deployed definitions and fails on any crossing not declared here.
